title: Why Leaves Change Color: Inside the Leaf

scenes.title: A LEAF IS A LIVING SYSTEM
scenes.caption: Color change begins inside leaf tissues.
scenes.narration: A leaf is made of many layers and cell types. As autumn develops, changes inside those tissues alter the colors we see.

scenes.title: CHLOROPLASTS CHANGE
scenes.caption: Photosynthetic structures are dismantled.
scenes.narration: As a tree prepares for winter, it dismantles parts of its photosynthetic system and recovers useful nutrients from the leaf.

scenes.title: NUTRIENTS ARE RECYCLED
scenes.caption: The tree reclaims valuable materials.
scenes.narration: Nitrogen and other nutrients are moved out of the leaf and stored in branches, trunks, and roots for future growth.

scenes.title: THE LEAF'S VASCULAR NETWORK
scenes.caption: Veins move water and sugars.
scenes.narration: Leaf veins contain transport tissues. They connect the leaf to the rest of the tree while the plant is active.

scenes.title: A CLOSING CONNECTION
scenes.caption: A separation layer develops near the stem.
scenes.narration: Near the base of the leaf, special cells form an abscission layer. This helps prepare the leaf to detach safely.

scenes.title: A CAREFUL SHUTDOWN
scenes.caption: The tree saves resources before winter.
scenes.narration: The color show is part of a practical process: reclaim nutrients, reduce water loss, and prepare the tree for cold conditions.
